solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Mix during school days, linger endlessly about (11)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: the word loses its end, its last letter
indicatorNotes.about: the letters are turned about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the school days of one teaching period make a term
LINGER without its last letter is LINGE, rearranged as INGLE

annotation.surface: Pupils mixing during term time and hanging around aimlessly afterwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mix' sits at the front looking like the start of the surface sentence, but it is the whole definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things that intermingle are mixed in together, as crowds do.

entries.clue: Reconstructed tiny landing in mad style (11)

indicatorNotes.Reconstructed: built again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters of TINY LANDING rearranged

annotation.surface: A cramped landing has been rebuilt in some crazy style.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mad' here means angry, the American sense, not crazy as the building work suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: To act indignantly is to act angrily, in a mad style.

entries.clue: Nervous retiring slow information technology (5)

indicatorNotes.retiring: going back, so the letters run backwards, upwards in a down clue

blocks.note: IT is the usual abbreviation for information technology

annotation.surface: Someone shy is intimidated by slow computer systems.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like part of the definition, since shy people are retiring, but it tells you to write DIM IT backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Timid means nervous and easily frightened.

entries.clue: Controlled endless royal household bitterness (7)

indicatorNotes.endless: without its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: to run a business is to control it
COURT, the royal household, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Resentment simmering inside a tightly run royal household.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like palace gossip; 'Controlled' is just the past tense RAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rancour is bitterness that has festered over time.

entries.clue: Move carefully in check (4)

blocks.note: CH is the chess notation for check

annotation.surface: A chess player moves a piece cautiously while their king is under attack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In check' reads as a single idea, restrained, but splits into IN plus the chess abbreviation CH.
annotation.definitionFit: To inch is to move slowly and carefully, a little at a time.

entries.clue: Complain audibly after spirit in drink (6,4)

indicatorNotes.audibly: said out loud, so the word is spelt as it sounds
indicatorNotes.after: this part comes after the first piece

blocks.note: to whine is to complain; WINE sounds the same

annotation.surface: Someone moans loudly after downing a shot of spirit in their drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' next to 'drink' suggests gin or whisky, but it is ginger in the sense of pep.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: ginger wine is a sweet fortified wine flavoured with ginger, drunk in winter or with whisky.

entries.clue: Gibson perhaps very tense over axe? (8,6)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

blocks.note: an electric atmosphere is very tense
axe is musicians' slang for a guitar

annotation.surface: Is someone called Gibson anxious about an axe, perhaps being sacked?
annotation.walkthrough: Gibson is the American guitar maker, so 'perhaps' marks a definition by example. 'Axe' looks like a chopping tool or a job cut.
annotation.definitionFit: Gibson's Les Paul is one of the best-known electric guitars.

entries.clue: Knowledgeable former fairy close outside church (11)

indicatorNotes.outside: the word for close goes outside CE

blocks.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian myth
CE = Church of England; it goes inside END

annotation.surface: A retired fairy, now wise, lives near a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close' reads as nearby, but it is the noun meaning end. PERI is a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone experienced knows a lot from having done it.

entries.clue: Register of names, rough but not right, written up for teacher? (8)

indicatorNotes.but not right: 'but' means except, so the word is taken without its R, the abbreviation for right
indicatorNotes.written up: in a down clue, written from the bottom up, so backwards

blocks.note: a rota is a list of names taking turns

annotation.surface: A teacher writes up a messy register of names.
annotation.walkthrough: ROTA plus CUDE, reversed, gives the answer; the register-and-teacher picture makes 'written up' look like note-taking.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: an educator is someone whose job is teaching.

entries.clue: Hippy Londoner partly observed temple gateway (5)

indicatorNotes.partly observed: only part of the words is seen, so the answer sits inside them

annotation.surface: A hippie from London is seen at the entrance of a temple.
annotation.walkthrough: Pylon usually means an electricity mast; its older sense is the grand gateway of an Egyptian temple.
annotation.definitionFit: In Egyptian architecture a pylon is the massive gateway to a temple.

entries.clue: Bicycle that’s unusual around city taken by criminal (9)

indicatorNotes.around: RUM goes around the city letters
indicatorNotes.taken by: the result is taken on by BENT, which follows it

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London; it goes inside RUM

annotation.surface: An odd-looking bicycle is stolen in the city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's unusual' seems to describe the bicycle, but it is the wordplay RUM. A recumbent is ridden lying back.
annotation.definitionFit: A recumbent is a bicycle ridden in a reclining position.

entries.clue: English allow catching silver bird (6)

indicatorNotes.catching: LET catches AG, holding it inside

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver; it goes inside LET

annotation.surface: An English person lets someone catch a silver-coloured bird.
annotation.walkthrough: AG comes from the Latin argentum.
annotation.definitionFit: A general word for a specific one: the eaglet is an eagle chick, still a bird.

entries.clue: People with film music (7,3,7)

blocks.note: a country is a people, a nation
a western is a cowboy film

annotation.surface: People watching a film with a soundtrack.
annotation.walkthrough: Short words each stand for a whole word of the answer; 'with' becomes AND.
annotation.definitionFit: Country and western is a genre of American popular music.

entries.clue: Slight daughter and I are abrasive with others regularly over years (11)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every second letter of the word is taken
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit over the Y

blocks.note: to scour is to rub abrasively

annotation.surface: A slight daughter and her parent are rude to other people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slight' at the front reads as small in build, but it is the noun, an insult.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun sense of slight: a snub or insult is a piece of rudeness.

entries.clue: Country friar getting God involved in the community (9,8)

blocks.note: a Dominican is a friar of the order of St Dominic
Re, or Ra, is the Egyptian sun god

annotation.surface: A country friar gets religion involved in local community life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country' seems to describe the friar, but it is the definition. RE is the Egyptian god.
annotation.definitionFit: The Dominican Republic is the Caribbean country sharing Hispaniola with Haiti.

entries.clue: Unit of fighting Aussies? (5)

blocks.note: the surface reading: a military unit, such as a platoon of Australian soldiers
the setter's reading: a unit of measurement in physics, with the Aussies joke flagged by the question mark

annotation.surface: A question about a military unit of Australian soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue looks like it wants an army unit such as a platoon of Australians; the question mark admits the play on words. The unit is scientific, and GAUSS looks like AUSS(IES) with a G.
annotation.definitionFit: The gauss is the CGS unit of magnetic flux density.

entries.clue: Continue without key speaker initially — one with sponsor? (6)

indicatorNotes.without: outside, so GO ON goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so only the first letter of the word is used

annotation.surface: A speech carries on without its main speaker, someone with a sponsor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking. A godparent was historically called a sponsor at baptism.
annotation.definitionFit: A godson has godparents, who sponsor him at his baptism.

entries.clue: Check concerning injury (8)

blocks.note: a strain is an injury to a muscle

annotation.surface: A medical check about an injury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as an examination, but it is the verb meaning hold back.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb sense of check: to hold something back, as you check or rein in a horse.

entries.clue: Conductor of energy in transmitter radio’s covering (7)

indicatorNotes.in: E goes inside the word for transmitter
indicatorNotes.covering: the cover of a word is its outside letters

blocks.note: a transmitter mast; E goes inside it

annotation.surface: A conductor of electrical energy inside a radio transmitter's casing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about electricity, so 'Conductor' seems to mean a wire; it is a musical conductor.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical conductor is often addressed as maestro, the Italian for master.

entries.clue: Bird’s bright red with head of orange (8)

indicatorNotes.head of: the head is the top or front, so the first letter of the word

annotation.surface: A bird is bright red with an orange head.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface describes the flamingo itself, which is pink with some orange.
annotation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a tall pink wading bird.

entries.clue: Great wolf running in late light (9)

indicatorNotes.running: the letters run about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters of GREAT WOLF rearranged

annotation.surface: A large wolf running at dusk.
annotation.walkthrough: The wolf seems to be running through the evening light; 'running' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: An afterglow is the light left in the sky after sunset.

entries.clue: Culminate with emoticon designed for sending a signal? (17)

indicatorNotes.designed: the letters are designed into a new shape, so rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of CULMINATE and EMOTICON rearranged

annotation.surface: A message ends with a smiley face designed to send a signal.
annotation.walkthrough: The texting picture makes the answer feel in scene, which is what hides the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Telecommunication is the transmission of signals over a distance by wire or radio.

entries.clue: Besotted admirer of procrastinator’s credo? (8)

blocks.note: split into three short words, the motto of someone who always puts things off

annotation.surface: Someone besotted with the idea of putting things off.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition only works when the answer is split into I DO LATER; the question mark flags the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: An idolater worships someone or something blindly.

entries.clue: Opposed states beginning to engage (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

annotation.surface: Hostile nations starting to go to war.
annotation.walkthrough: 'States' reads as countries, but it is the verb: he avers.
annotation.definitionFit: Opposed to and averse to are used the same way: you are averse to or opposed to an idea.

entries.clue: Horrible-sounding textile worker? (4)

indicatorNotes.sounding: the word as it sounds, not as spelt

blocks.note: dire = horrible; say it aloud and it matches a trade that colours cloth

annotation.surface: A textile worker whose name sounds awful.
annotation.walkthrough: Dire and dyer sound the same, so the horrible-sounding worker is the one who colours cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: A dyer colours cloth, a textile trade.

entries.clue: British composer almost entirely joyous (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: nearly all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: Sir Arthur Bliss was a British composer, Master of the Queen's Music

annotation.surface: A British composer who is nearly always cheerful.
annotation.walkthrough: BLISS is also a word for joy, which makes the surface feel like a definition throughout.
annotation.definitionFit: Blissful means full of joy.

entries.clue: Ram eating half of lily flower (5)

indicatorNotes.eating: TUP takes the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.half of: half the letters of the word

blocks.note: the first half of LILY; it goes inside TUP

annotation.surface: A ram munching part of a lily flower.
annotation.walkthrough: TUP is a dialect word for a ram, common in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tulip is one kind of flower.

entries.clue: Turning up shoddy stuff I have alleged (8)

indicatorNotes.Turning: turn UP round so it reads backwards

annotation.surface: Someone claims to have found cheap junk turning up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reads as appearing, but 'Turning' acts on the word 'up' itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a putative father is the one generally supposed to be the father.

entries.clue: Run miles, taking a long time (6)

annotation.surface: A slow runner taking ages to cover the miles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run' starts the sentence as a command to jog, but it is the definition, as in run a business.
annotation.definitionFit: The business sense of run: to run a shop is to be in charge of it.

entries.clue: Way to get over fence being protected by coppers in corruption (10)

indicatorNotes.being protected by: surrounded by the word for coppers

blocks.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence
coppers are copper coins, pennies; STILE goes inside PENCE

annotation.surface: A way over the fence guarded by corrupt police officers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police, but it is copper coins. Pestilence can mean something morally corrupting.
annotation.definitionFit: Pestilence is a plague, and by extension anything that corrupts or destroys.

entries.clue: Unattractive quality of paleness destroyed with suntan (14)

indicatorNotes.destroyed: the letters are broken up and put back in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of PALENESS and SUNTAN rearranged

annotation.surface: A pale complexion ruined by a tan is not an attractive look.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes a beauty complaint of it; the whole wordplay is PALENESS plus SUNTAN rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: The -ness ending turns unpleasant into a quality, one that makes someone or something unattractive.

entries.clue: Unknown longing to seize time boating (8)

indicatorNotes.to seize: ACHING grabs T and holds it inside

blocks.note: Y is an unknown in algebra
T = time; it goes inside ACHING

annotation.surface: A mysterious longing to take time off for a boat trip.
annotation.walkthrough: X, Y and Z are the algebraic unknowns, and Y begins the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Yachting is the sport of sailing, a form of boating.

entries.clue: Big rock concealing grounds is basalt outcrop (6,8)

blocks.note: grounds for complaint are cause; it goes inside SWAY

annotation.surface: A large rock hiding the grounds is a basalt outcrop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock' is pure geology in the surface, but it is the verb meaning sway. The Giant's Causeway is a field of basalt columns on the coast of Northern Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: The Giant's Causeway is a famous outcrop of hexagonal basalt columns in County Antrim.

entries.clue: Physicist Dave Fogg made prof, giving up external positions? (8)

indicatorNotes.giving up external positions: each word loses its outside letters, leaving the middle

annotation.surface: A physicist named Dave Fogg is promoted to professor, giving up outside posts?
annotation.walkthrough: Dave Fogg is invented; the name exists only to supply letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the Italian physicist behind Avogadro's number.

entries.clue: Goodness one’s seen in Queen Victoria over a day (6)

indicatorNotes.seen in: I is inside the letters for Queen Victoria
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue the first piece sits over the day

blocks.note: VR = Victoria Regina, her royal cipher
I = one; it goes inside VR

annotation.surface: Goodness shown by Queen Victoria for a day.
annotation.walkthrough: VR stands for Victoria Regina, Latin for Queen Victoria.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: virtue is moral goodness.

entries.clue: Unsatisfied brick carrier in charge of colleague as if not organised (14)

blocks.note: a hod is a trough for carrying bricks

annotation.surface: A dissatisfied hod carrier runs a colleague's work in a chaotic way.
annotation.walkthrough: A hod is the builder's trough for carrying bricks on the shoulder.
annotation.definitionFit: To act unmethodically is to act as if without organisation.

entries.clue: University want to include x-ray patent that’s not yet illustrated (11)

indicatorNotes.to include: NEED takes the letters inside it

blocks.note: X-ray is X in the phonetic alphabet
patent = obvious, plain; X and PLAIN go inside NEED

annotation.surface: A university wants a patent that has no drawings yet to include an x-ray.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like an invention's legal protection but is the adjective meaning obvious; 'illustrated' means explained.
annotation.definitionFit: Something not yet illustrated in the sense of explained is unexplained.

entries.clue: Badly focused with name unclear (8)

indicatorNotes.Badly: the letters are put together badly, in a new order

blocks.note: N = name, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A blurry photo, badly focused, with the name impossible to read.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is itself about blurriness, so 'unclear' reads as a description, not the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A muddled or blurred account is confused, hard to make out.

entries.clue: Free day I got off to fish (11)

blocks.note: to get a letter off is to send it
to angle is to fish with a rod

annotation.surface: On my day off I went fishing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free day' reads as a holiday, but 'Free' is the verb and is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A knot or snare you undo sets something free, which is disentangling it.

entries.clue: What was produced by Midas touch is novel (10)

annotation.definition2: What was produced by Midas touch

blocks.clueFragment: What was produced by Midas touch
blocks.note: King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so his touching finger would be a gold one

annotation.surface: A book about the result of King Midas's touch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like it means new, but it is the book.
annotation.definitionFit: Goldfinger is Ian Fleming's 1959 James Bond novel.

entries.clue: Fence put round a quiet cove (10)

indicatorNotes.put round: the letters are moved round into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters of A QUIET COVE rearranged

annotation.surface: A fence is built around a secluded bay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fence' is the verb from fencing: to parry questions and dodge a straight answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To fence with questions is to equivocate, avoiding a direct answer.

entries.clue: Admitted being knocked out with iron, not copper (9)

indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means along with, so the iron symbol is brought into the word
indicatorNotes.not: 'not copper' excludes copper, so its symbol is taken out to make room

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron; it replaces CU
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; it is taken out

annotation.surface: A boxer admits to being knocked out by an iron bar rather than a copper one.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the CU in CONCUSSED for FE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for owning up: the suspect admitted, or confessed, to the crime.

entries.clue: God’s not started in incomplete heathen temple (6)

indicatorNotes.not started: a word that has not started is missing its beginning, its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: the remaining letters go inside the next word
indicatorNotes.incomplete: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: PAGAN without its last letter; OD goes inside it

annotation.surface: A god is absent from a half-built pagan temple.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is read as 'is': God is not started, giving OD.
annotation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered temple of East Asia.

entries.clue: City guides reported (5)

indicatorNotes.reported: said out loud, so spelt as it sounds

annotation.surface: City guides have filed a report.
annotation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the city is the largest in Yorkshire, northern England.

entries.clue: Immorality surrounding a kid minister’s housing (8)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: VICE goes round the other letters

blocks.note: to kid is to tease, to rag; A RAG goes inside VICE

annotation.surface: Scandal surrounds a child in a minister's household.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child, but it is the verb meaning tease.
annotation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a vicar, a church minister.

entries.clue: Proper sort of number, one short (4)

indicatorNotes.one short: one letter short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a prime is a sort of number; drop the last letter

annotation.surface: The right kind of number, with one missing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Proper sort of number' reads as one phrase, but 'Proper' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Prim describes someone stiffly correct, a little too proper.

entries.clue: A nice gal? Could be (8)

indicatorNotes.Could be: the letters could be arranged into something else

blocks.note: the eight letters of A NICE GAL rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether the girl in question is nice.
annotation.walkthrough: Angelica is a girl's name, so the whole clue both describes and spells her.
annotation.definitionFit: Angelica is a girl's name, and a nice gal could well be called it.

entries.clue: Musketeer’s name not available during reinforcement (9)

indicatorNotes.during: these letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: a tag is a name, as on a name tag
a darn reinforces a worn sock; TAG NA goes inside it

annotation.surface: A musketeer's name is missing while reinforcements arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Musketeer's name' seems to ask for a name, but the ’s is 'has' and 'name' is the wordplay TAG.
annotation.definitionFit: D'Artagnan is the hero who joins Dumas's Three Musketeers.

entries.clue: Lacking map missing church is simple (7)

annotation.surface: Getting lost without a map or a church landmark is a simple mistake.
annotation.walkthrough: CH is the standard abbreviation for church.
annotation.definitionFit: Artless means simple, without guile.

entries.clue: Agree man’s breaking heart (6)

indicatorNotes.breaking: HE breaks into the word for heart

blocks.note: the core is the heart; HE goes inside it

annotation.surface: Agreeing that a man's heart is breaking.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is': man is breaking heart.
annotation.definitionFit: Arguments or accounts that cohere hang together and agree with each other.

entries.clue: Sailor abandoned seafood (7)

annotation.surface: A shipwrecked sailor left eating shellfish.
annotation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the commonest sailor in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail.

entries.clue: Insect found in straight banana (8)

indicatorNotes.found in: the insect is found inside the next word

blocks.note: plain = straight, honest; ANT goes inside it

annotation.surface: A bug discovered inside a perfectly straight banana.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Straight banana' sounds like a fruit description, but 'straight' is the wordplay PLAIN.
annotation.definitionFit: The starchy cooking plantain belongs to the banana family, a definition by category.

entries.clue: Empty pie tin which could be used for a pie (5)

annotation.definition: which could be used for a pie
annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the answer as a filling rather than naming it

indicatorNotes.Empty: emptied of its inside, leaving the outer letters

annotation.surface: An empty pie tin waiting to be used for baking.
annotation.walkthrough: The pie and tin both seem part of the baking scene, but the definition is the filling.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the nut is the filling of the American pecan pie.

entries.clue: Way to precede lowlife with A levels (6)

indicatorNotes.to precede: ST comes before the next piece

annotation.surface: A way for a lowlife to get ahead with A levels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A levels' are British school exams; here the A is wordplay and 'levels' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Geology's rock layers, or society's classes, are levels one above another.

entries.clue: One mum served up good old china? (5)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, sent upwards, so written backwards

annotation.surface: A mother serves up the good old china.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' is rhyming slang: china plate means mate, so china is a friend, not crockery; 'good old' gives G and O.
annotation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, as china is slang for mate.

entries.clue: Cut cakes up (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, written upwards, so backwards

annotation.surface: Cutting cakes into pieces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as slicing the cakes, but it means ignore someone deliberately.
annotation.definitionFit: The social sense of cut: to cut someone dead is to ignore them on purpose.

entries.clue: Sound of hooter enveloping one (5)

indicatorNotes.enveloping: an envelope wraps its contents, so the word is wrapped round the letter

blocks.note: I = one; it goes inside NOSE

annotation.surface: The sound of a car horn wrapping around someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn, which fits 'Sound', but it is British slang for a nose.
annotation.definitionFit: The general sense of noise: any sound, not just an unwelcome one.

entries.clue: Way of changing people’s profession following party (6,11)

indicatorNotes.following: the profession comes after the party

annotation.surface: Someone changes career after a party.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'people's profession' looks like one phrase but is not.
annotation.definitionFit: Social engineering is the attempt to change attitudes and behaviour across society.

entries.clue: Function can end in red getting drunk (6,5)

indicatorNotes.getting drunk: drunk letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters of CAN END IN RED rearranged

annotation.surface: A party that can end with red wine flowing and guests drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as a purpose or maths term, but here it is a formal social event.
annotation.definitionFit: A dinner dance is a social function with a meal and dancing.

entries.clue: Scene’s first in sci-fi movie in weird set which lights up regularly (11)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a descriptive clause for the device rather than a noun

indicatorNotes.first: the first part of the scene, so its opening letter
indicatorNotes.in: the letters go inside the next word
indicatorNotes.weird: the letters are made weird, rearranged

blocks.note: the 1987 film RoboCop; S goes inside it
SET rearranged; ROBOSCOP goes inside it

annotation.surface: A scene from a sci-fi film shot on a strange set lit by flashing lights.
annotation.walkthrough: RoboCop is the 1987 sci-fi film about a cyborg police officer; two containers nest inside each other here.
annotation.definitionFit: A stroboscope is a lamp that flashes at regular intervals.
